title: Three arrested over alleged sale of in fake motorcycle, tricycle number plates Niger
text:
The Niger State Police Command has arrested three suspects over the alleged production and sale of counterfeit motorcycle
has arrested three suspects over the alleged production and sale of counterfeit motorcycle and tricycle number plates in Suleja Local Government Area of the state.
The suspects, identified as Obinna Sunday, 21, of Rafin-Sanyi, Suleja; Sunday Fajobi, 71, of Jubilee Road, Suleja; and Aisha Ismail, 41, also of Jubilee Road, Suleja, were arrested following a complaint over fake number plates found on tricycles operated by a leasing company in the area. According to the command’s spokesman, Superintendent of Police Wasiu Abiodun, the complaint was lodged at the Maje Police Division, Suleja, on September 29, 2026, after officials of the Vehicle Inspection Office raised concerns about the authenticity of number plates on tricycles belonging to the company.
Abiodun said the complaint prompted detectives at the division to commence an investigation, which led to the arrest of the three suspects. He said preliminary investigation indicated that Sunday and Fajobi allegedly posed as VIO officials and facilitated the sale of more than 60 counterfeit motorcycle and tricycle number plates bearing Kaduna and Nasarawa State inscriptions to unsuspecting operators.
Police said a search of one of the suspects’ premises also led to the recovery of 10 newly printed counterfeit motorcycle and tricycle number plates bearing Kano State. Other items recovered, according to the command, included 61 fake motorcycle and tricycle number plates, two laptop computers, two electronic printing machines, fake insurance documents allegedly used in registering the plates and N870,000 suspected to be proceeds of theThe police said interrogation of the suspects produced further leads.
Obinna allegedly confessed to purchasing the counterfeit plates from Aisha for N40,000, while Aisha reportedly admitted selling the plates to him after obtaining them from one Bala Ibrahim, who she identified as an alleged VIO officer serving in Abuja. The command said the suspects had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, Minna, where they were being detained while investigations continued.
The police did not disclose whether the alleged VIO officer had been officially confirmed as an employee of the agency.
